```{r}
# helper function to label PI curve data type.
modified_DataType_piCurve <- function(df) {
  tibble(
    data_type = DataType_piCurve(data = df)$data_type,
    index_id = unique(df$index_id)
  )
}
```

```{r}
## original cleaned data from M
og_path <-  "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/pe_curves/mohammad/data/cleaned-data/testData/pro_hourly_growth_par-cleaned-MA-Aug6-2026.csv"
setwd("/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/pe_curves/notebooks")

# new data I generated 
time_res <- '30min'
filter_type <- 'savgol'

path <- glue(
    "/Users/Kathy/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-UW/Desktop/UW/projects/",
    "pe_curves/data/smoothed_growth_data/clean_growth_{time_res}_{filter_type}.csv"
  )

df_main <- read.csv(path) |>
  # change "time" col to "datetime"
  rename(datetime = time) |>
  # create new cols for year, month, and day
  mutate(
    datetime = ymd_hms(datetime),
    time = format(datetime, "%H:%M:%S"),
    yr = year(datetime),
    mnth = month(datetime),
    dy = day(datetime)
  ) |>
  # drop original index col
  select(-X) |>
  # group by each cruise, day, and population to generate integer labels for each curve
  group_by(cruise, cruise_day, pop) |>
  mutate(
    index_id = paste0("pi-", cur_group_id())
  ) |>
  ungroup() # removes grouping structure
# so far data looks good 

# print # of pi groups
cat(
    "Time resolution: ", time_res,
    " | Total PI groups: ",
    n_distinct(df_main$index_id),
    "\n",
    sep = ""
  )
# Only keep the first 8 hours of each day and rename PI-model columns
max_hours = 8
df_renamed <- df_main |>
  filter(hour <= 8) |>
  # rename cols for PI curve model
  rename(
    P = slope,
    I = norm_par_smooth
  ) |>
  mutate(
    time_res = time_res
  )
# Split data into one data frame per PI curve
df_sub <- df_renamed |>
  group_by(index_id) |>
  group_split()

# Label each PI curve, then retain time-resolution metadata.
df_label <- parallel::mclapply(
    df_sub,
    function(x) modified_DataType_piCurve(df = x),
    mc.cores = 13
  ) |>
    bind_rows() |>
    mutate(
      time_res = time_res
    )

# count the number of data types by time resolution
df_label |>
  count(time_res, data_type) |>
  group_by(time_res) |>
  mutate(
    perc = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
  
# most datasets are uncertain and light limited for 1H data
```

Helper function to upweight low irradiance values
```{r}
upweight_low_light <- function(
  df,
  irradiance_col = "I",
  low_I_min = 0,
  low_I_max = 1000,
  low_I_weight = 3
) {
  # Keep all observations once.
  df_weighted <- df

  # Identify observations to replicate.
  low_I_rows <- df |>
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[irradiance_col]]),
      .data[[irradiance_col]] >= low_I_min,
      .data[[irradiance_col]] <= low_I_max
    )

  # Add extra copies. For weight = 3, each low-I observation appears 3 times total.
  if (nrow(low_I_rows) > 0 && low_I_weight > 1) {
    df_weighted <- bind_rows(
      df,
      low_I_rows[rep(seq_len(nrow(low_I_rows)), each = low_I_weight - 1), ]
    )
  }

  df_weighted
}
```

## TESTING (diel cruise only)
```{r}
# Lists to hold successful fit results and plot objects.
fit_par_list <- list()
weight <- 3

# run only on diel cruise now
test_diel <- subset(df_renamed, (cruise == 'KM1513' & pop == 'prochloro')) |> 
  arrange(cruise_day, hour)

# loop through eacy population
for (curr_pop in unique(df_renamed$pop)) {
  # subset population DF
  pop_df <- subset(test_diel, pop == curr_pop)
  # group by cruise day and index ID
  df_sub <- pop_df |>
      group_by(cruise_day, index_id) |>
      group_split()
  # loop through each PI curve and save data 
  for (i in seq_along(df_sub)) {
      df <- df_sub[[i]]
      
      # Extract one value for each curve-level metadata field.
      index_id_i <- unique(df$index_id)[1]
      cruise_i <- unique(df$cruise)[1]
      cruise_day_i <- unique(df$cruise_day)[1]
      pop_i <- curr_pop
      
      # skip if not enough data per curve (at least 4 hours of data)
      if (nrow(df) <= 4) {
        message(
          "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
          ": fewer than 5 rows"
        )
        next
      }
      # set weights for low light levels
      df_weighted <- upweight_low_light(
          df,
          irradiance_col = "I",
          low_I_min = 0,
          low_I_max = 250,
          low_I_weight = weight
      )
      tryCatch({
        # # run weighted fit in PI model
        # fit <- Fit_piModel(
        #     data = df_weighted,
        #     STATapp = "MSE"
        #   )
        
        fit <- Fit_piModel(
          data = df_weighted,
          DarkReactionRate_R = T,
          Control = list(maxit = 5000)
        )

        # Store fitted parameter results.
        fit_par_list[[length(fit_par_list) + 1]] <- tibble(
            index_id = index_id_i,
            cruise = cruise_i,
            cruise_day = cruise_day_i,
            pop = pop_i,
            n_obs = nrow(df),
            Pmax = unname(fit$par["Pmax"]),
            alpha = unname(fit$par["alpha"]),
            beta = unname(fit$par["beta"])
          )
        # plot PI curve  
        p <- Plot_piCurve(
            fit,
            df_weighted,
            length_out = 200,
            n_cores = 6
          ) +
          labs(
            title = paste("Pop:", curr_pop, "Day:", cruise_day_i),
            subtitle = as.character(index_id_i),
            y = expression("Growth Rate" ~ (hour^{-1}))
          )  +
            theme(
              axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
              axis.title = element_text(size = 14)
            )
        print(p + # increase the size of axis title and font
        theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 14), axis.title = element_text(size = 14)))
      }, error = function(e) {
      message(
        "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
        ": ", conditionMessage(e)
        )}
    )
  }
}
```

```{r}
  )
```

## Run through all populations and cruises
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# Settings
weight <- 3
ncols <- 4
output_dir <- "../figures/pi_curves"

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Include all cruises and populations.
test_diel <- df_renamed |>
  filter(!is.na(cruise), !is.na(pop)) |>
  arrange(pop, cruise, cruise_day, hour)

# Helper: make filename-safe population labels.
safe_filename <- function(x) {
  gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", as.character(x))
}

# helper function to save PDF after loop closes
write_population_pdf <- function(plots, filename, width, height) {

  if (length(plots) == 0L) {
    stop("No cruise plots available to save.")
  }

  grDevices::pdf(
    file = filename,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    onefile = TRUE
  )

  pdf_device <- grDevices::dev.cur()

  # Close this particular device if printing fails.
  on.exit({
    if (pdf_device %in% grDevices::dev.list()) {
      try(
        grDevices::dev.off(which = pdf_device),
        silent = TRUE
      )
    }
  }, add = TRUE)

  for (cruise_name in names(plots)) {

    message("Writing PDF page: ", cruise_name)

    grDevices::dev.set(which = pdf_device)
    print(plots[[cruise_name]])
  }

  # Explicitly finalize the PDF before reporting success.
  grDevices::dev.off(which = pdf_device)
}

# Extract realized (observed) PI parameters from the predicted curve in a Plot_piCurve() plot.
extract_observed_pars <- function(p, low_frac = 0.1) {

  built <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)$data
  # Use the layer with the most points (the 200-point prediction line).
  n_pts <- vapply(built, nrow, integer(1))
  curve <- built[[which.max(n_pts)]] |>
    dplyr::filter(is.finite(x), is.finite(y)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(x) |>
    dplyr::summarise(y = mean(y), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::arrange(x)

  i_max     <- which.max(curve$y)
  Pmax_obs  <- curve$y[i_max]
  I_at_Pmax <- curve$x[i_max]

  # Initial slope: linear fit over the lowest low_frac of the irradiance range (I >= 0).
  pos <- curve |> dplyr::filter(x >= 0)
  low <- pos |> dplyr::filter(x <= min(x) + low_frac * diff(range(x)))
  alpha_obs <- if (nrow(low) >= 3) unname(coef(lm(y ~ x, data = low))[2]) else NA_real_

  # Photoinhibition: slope of the curve beyond the peak (positive = decline).
  post <- curve[i_max:nrow(curve), ]
  beta_obs <- if (nrow(post) >= 3 && diff(range(post$x)) > 0) {
    -unname(coef(lm(y ~ x, data = post))[2])
  } else NA_real_

  tibble(
    Pmax_obs  = Pmax_obs,
    I_at_Pmax = I_at_Pmax,
    alpha_obs = alpha_obs,
    beta_obs  = beta_obs,
    Ik_obs    = Pmax_obs / alpha_obs
  )
}

# Process one population and save all cruise pages in one PDF.
plot_population_pdf <- function(pop_data, curr_pop) {

  fit_par_list <- list()
  cruise_plot_list <- list()

  # Calculate limits using all cruises for this population.
  I_values <- pop_data$I[is.finite(pop_data$I)]
  P_values <- pop_data$P[is.finite(pop_data$P)]

  if (length(I_values) == 0 || length(P_values) == 0) {
    stop("No finite I or P values for population: ", curr_pop)
  }

  # Include zero and retain negative values if present.
  x_range <- range(c(0, I_values))
  y_range <- range(c(0, P_values))

  # Add a little headroom; handle an all-zero range.
  x_span <- diff(x_range)
  y_span <- diff(y_range)

  x_limits <- c(
    -100,
    x_range[2] + if (x_span > 0) 0.05 * x_span else 1
  )

  y_limits <- c(
    -0.01,
    y_range[2] + if (y_span > 0) 0.10 * y_span else 0.01
  )

  # Determine a common page size for this population's PDF.
  # Each cruise will occupy exactly one page.
  panel_counts <- pop_data |>
    distinct(cruise, cruise_day, index_id) |>
    count(cruise, name = "n_panels")

  max_panels <- max(panel_counts$n_panels)
  max_rows <- ceiling(max_panels / ncols)
  # Make population name safe for file names.
  pop_file_name <- gsub(
      pattern = "[^A-Za-z0-9_-]",
      replacement = "_",
      x = as.character(curr_pop)
    )
    # set file name
  pdf_file <- paste0(
      pop_file_name,
      "_",
      "weight",
      weight,
      ".pdf"
    )
  output_file <- file.path(
    output_dir,
    paste0("PI_curves_", pdf_file)
  )

  grDevices::pdf(
    file = output_file,
    width = 4 * ncols,
    height = max(6, 3 * max_rows + 1.5),
    onefile = TRUE
  )

  # Ensure the PDF closes even if an unexpected error occurs.
  on.exit(grDevices::dev.off(), add = TRUE)

  cruise_ids <- sort(unique(pop_data$cruise))

  for (curr_cruise in cruise_ids) {

    message(
      "Processing population: ", curr_pop,
      " | Cruise: ", curr_cruise
    )

    # Create one group per daily PI curve.
    # Group keys determine panel order: cruise_day, then index_id.
    df_sub <- pop_data |>
      filter(cruise == curr_cruise) |>
      group_by(cruise_day, index_id) |>
      group_split(.keep = TRUE)

    daily_plot_list <- list()

    for (i in seq_along(df_sub)) {

      df <- df_sub[[i]] |>
        arrange(hour)

      index_id_i <- df$index_id[1]
      cruise_day_i <- df$cruise_day[1]

      # Retain your original minimum-row requirement.
      if (nrow(df) <= 4) {
        message(
          "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
          ": fewer than 5 rows"
        )
        next
      }

      result <- tryCatch({

        # Upweight low-light observations.
        df_weighted <- upweight_low_light(
          df,
          irradiance_col = "I",
          low_I_min = 0,
          low_I_max = 250,
          low_I_weight = weight
        )

        # Retain your current model-fitting settings.
        fit <- Fit_piModel(
          data = df_weighted,
          DarkReactionRate_R = TRUE,
          Control = list(maxit = 5000)
        )

        # Create the individual daily panel.
        p <- Plot_piCurve(
          fit,
          df_weighted,
          length_out = 200,
          n_cores = 1
        ) +
          labs(
            title = paste("Day:", cruise_day_i),
            subtitle = as.character(index_id_i),
            y = expression("Growth Rate" ~ (hour^{-1}))
          ) +
          coord_cartesian(
            xlim = x_limits,
            ylim = y_limits,
            expand = FALSE
          ) +
          theme(
            plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 10)
          )

        # Build the parameter row only after fit and plot succeed.
        # Fitted (model) parameters plus realized (observed) parameters.
        obs_pars <- extract_observed_pars(p)

        all_fit <- as.list(fit$par)
        names(all_fit) <- paste0("par_", names(all_fit))

        fit_pars <- bind_cols(
          tibble(
            index_id   = index_id_i,
            cruise     = curr_cruise,
            cruise_day = cruise_day_i,
            pop        = curr_pop,
            n_obs      = nrow(df),
            Pmax_fit   = unname(fit$par["Pmax"]),
            alpha_fit  = unname(fit$par["alpha"]),
            beta_fit   = unname(fit$par["beta"])
          ),
          obs_pars,
          as_tibble(all_fit)
        )

        list(plot = p, parameters = fit_pars)

      }, error = function(e) {

        message(
          "Skipping curve ", index_id_i,
          ": ", conditionMessage(e)
        )

        NULL
      })

      if (is.null(result)) {
        next
      }

      daily_plot_list[[length(daily_plot_list) + 1]] <- result$plot

      fit_par_list[[length(fit_par_list) + 1]] <-
        result$parameters
    }

    # Build one combined plot for this cruise.
    if (length(daily_plot_list) > 0) {

      cruise_plot <- (
        wrap_plots(
          daily_plot_list,
          ncol = ncols,
          guides = "collect"
        ) +
          plot_annotation(
            title = paste(
              "Cruise:", curr_cruise,
              "| Population:", curr_pop
            ),
            subtitle = paste(
              "Low-light weight:", weight,
              "| Panels ordered by cruise day"
            ),
            theme = theme(
              plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
              plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11)
            )
          )
      ) &
        theme(legend.position = "bottom")

    } else {

      # Preserve one page per cruise even if all fits fail.
      cruise_plot <- ggplot() +
        annotate(
          "text",
          x = 0,
          y = 0,
          label = "No successful PI curve fits",
          size = 6
        ) +
        labs(
          title = paste(
            "Cruise:", curr_cruise,
            "| Population:", curr_pop
          )
        ) +
        theme_void()
    }
    # store each cruise plot 
    cruise_plot_list[[as.character(curr_cruise)]] <- cruise_plot
  }

  # # This runs AFTER the cruise loop has finished.
  # write_population_pdf(
  #   plots = cruise_plot_list,
  #   filename = output_file,
  #   width = 4 * ncols,
  #   height = max(6, 3 * max_rows + 1.5)
  # )

  message("Finished PDF: ", output_file)

  bind_rows(fit_par_list)
}

# Run once per population.
fit_par_list <- list()

populations <- sort(unique(test_diel$pop))

for (curr_pop in populations) {

  pop_df <- test_diel |>
    filter(pop == curr_pop)

  fit_par_list[[as.character(curr_pop)]] <-
    plot_population_pdf(
      pop_data = pop_df,
      curr_pop = curr_pop
    )
}



# Combine successful parameter results from all populations and cruises.
fit_par_df <- bind_rows(fit_par_list)
```

# Plot distributions of observed PI parameters

```{r}
library(tidyr)

# Calculate Ek from the observed parameters
fit_par_df$Ek_obs <- fit_par_df$Pmax_obs / fit_par_df$alpha_obs

# Convert observed parameters from wide to long
fit_par_long <- fit_par_df %>%
  select(-any_of(c("Pmax_fit", "alpha_fit", "beta_fit", "Ek_fit"))) %>%  # avoid name clashes with fitted columns
  rename(
    Pmax  = Pmax_obs,
    alpha = alpha_obs,
    beta  = beta_obs,
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Pmax, alpha, Ek_obs, beta),
    names_to = "parameter",
    values_to = "estimate"
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(estimate)) %>%
  mutate(
    time_res = factor(
      time_res,
      levels = c("3min", "15min", "30min", "1H")
    ),
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c("Pmax", "alpha", "beta", "Ek_obs")
    )
  )

# Log-transform (only positive values can be logged)
fit_par_log_long <- fit_par_long %>%
  filter(estimate > 0) %>%
  mutate(log_estimate = log(estimate))

# Save as CSV files
```

```{r}
  geom_density(
    fill = "#2C7FB8",
    color = "#08519C",
    alpha = 0.30,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    adjust = 1
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    pop ~ parameter,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +
  ggh4x::facetted_pos_scales(
    x = list(
      parameter == "beta" ~ scale_x_continuous(
        limits = c(-15, -5)  # Example upper limit; replace as needed
      )
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed P–I parameter distributions across Populations",
    x = "Log (parameter estimate)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.9, "lines")
  )
```

### Now let's try the new model (Code from Mohammad)
```{r}
# functions
fit_2tanh_model <- function(x) {
  fit_noDR <- Fit_piModel(data = x, Control = list(maxit = 5000))
  
  fit <- Fit_piModel(
    data = x,
    DarkReactionRate_R = T,
    Control = list(maxit = 5000)
  )
  
  
  tidy_output <-
    function(model, data = x) {
      params <- model$par
      mse <- model$value
      sqa <- model$SQA
      
      c(index_id = unique(x$index_id),
        params,
        mse = mse,
        sqa)
    }
  
  if (fit_noDR$SQA["R2"] >= fit$SQA["R2adj"]) {
    tidy_output(model = fit_noDR)
  } else{
    tidy_output(model = fit)
  }
}
```


